## backdown service install {#install}

Install and start the daemon as a systemd service (a user service unless --system)

```text
backdown service install [OPTIONS]
```

### Options

`--system`
: Machine-wide service running as the `backdown` user (needs sudo).

`--no-start`
: Install but don't start it.

`--print`
: Print the unit file instead of installing it.

## backdown service uninstall {#uninstall}

Stop and remove the service (the index is kept)

```text
backdown service uninstall [OPTIONS]
```

### Options

`--system`
: &nbsp;

## backdown service status {#status}

Is the service installed and running, and what is it doing?

```text
backdown service status [OPTIONS]
```

### Options

`--system`
: &nbsp;

All of them also take the [global options](/docs/cli/#global-options) `--db` and `--local`.

## Good to know

On Linux, a systemd user service that runs as you; with `--system`, a machine-wide service that runs as a `backdown` user that can read every file and write none, with no network beyond this machine (add people to the `backdown` group to let them use it). On macOS {preview}, a LaunchAgent that runs while you're logged in (its log is in `~/Library/Logs/BackDown`). On Windows {preview}, a scheduled task "BackDown" that starts it, hidden, when you log on. `--system` is Linux-only. Uninstalling keeps the index.

## Examples

```sh
backdown service install
backdown service status
# see what it would install first
backdown service install --print
# machine-wide, on Linux (NAS, server)
sudo backdown service install --system
backdown service uninstall
```
